metadata.dataset: Barpeta district historical disaster context and critical infrastructure

historical_floods: ASDMA (Assam State Disaster Management Authority) -- Flood Situation Reports 2022-2023. asdma.assam.gov.in
Sphere India, Assam Flood 2022 Assessment Report. sphereindia.org.in
sources.critical_infrastructure: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API (queried 2026-09-22). CC BY-SA 2.0.
sources.capacity_standard: NDMA Guidelines on Minimum Standards of Relief (2016). Section 3: Shelter. 3.5 sq.m covered area per person.

metadata.non_claims_note: Historical figures are from secondary sources (ASDMA situation reports, news reports citing ASDMA). They are cited for contextual awareness, not as verified census counts. Infrastructure data from OSM reflects volunteer-contributed mapping and may be incomplete.

historical_flood_context.flood_frequency: Annual -- Barpeta experiences severe riverine flooding every monsoon season (June-September) from the Brahmaputra and its tributaries (Manas, Beki, Pahumara, Kaldia).

recent_events.peak_affected_note: Reported peak by ASDMA: over 1.27 million people marooned in Barpeta district alone during the second wave (June 2022). Source: Sphere India 2022 assessment citing ASDMA situation reports.
recent_events.villages_inundated: Multiple waves; embankment breaches reported across the district.
recent_events.source: Sphere India / ASDMA Flood Situation Reports 2022

recent_events.peak_affected_note: ~65,221 people affected in Barpeta by late June 2023. ~93 villages affected, 225 hectares of cropland inundated. Source: NDTV citing ASDMA June 2023.
recent_events.source: NDTV / ASDMA Flood Situation Report June 2023

historical_flood_context.char_areas_note: Barpeta has numerous 'char' (riverine island) settlements that are disproportionately vulnerable. These are typically unconnected by road during floods.

critical_infrastructure_near_sites.note: All records from OSM Overpass query (bbox 26.20-26.50N, 90.80-91.10E, 2026-09-22). Only named features included. This list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

hospitals_and_clinics.name: Barpeta Medical College and Hospital, Barpeta
hospitals_and_clinics.note: Tertiary care -- primary trauma/emergency resource for Barpeta town. 0.9 km from SHL-001.

hospitals_and_clinics.name: Barpeta Road F.R.U
hospitals_and_clinics.note: First Referral Unit (FRU) -- surgical and obstetric capacity.

shelter_capacity_standard.standard: NDMA Guidelines on Minimum Standards of Relief (2016)
shelter_capacity_standard.citation: National Disaster Management Authority, India. Section 3 -- Shelter. Available: ndma.gov.in
shelter_capacity_standard.applicability_note: Applicable to all government relief camps established under the Disaster Management Act 2005. PMAY-G is a housing construction scheme, not a relief camp standard -- no PMAY-G capacity standard for shelters exists.
shelter_capacity_standard.covid_revision_source: Assam Government COVID-19 relief camp guidelines 2020. assam.gov.in
